liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire on the Mountain** (3 reviews): Slow, pleasant second-set opener; Weir sang a backing vocal off cue, while Jerry's vocals were spot-on; Stand-alone second-set opener, mellow, a standout; the show ended with a double encore [17][18][19]
- **It Must Have Been the Roses** (1 review): Jerry's thoughtful guitar solo inflections in this song stood out to the listener [21]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Slow, patient, almost ragtime staccato feel, with Brent's background vocals; a favorite version of the reviewer [24]
- **Truckin** (1 review): Bob's lead vocal on this song sounds weak to the reviewer [22]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Wild Bobby freakout in the 'Sweet Sweet Summertime' Lovelight, with strong echo delays from Healy [26]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 review): Jerry sounds fine, Bob is okay on backing vocals, and the band played well [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-06-22.schoeps.grace-szvetecz.gems.100204.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1986-06-22.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81646.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd86-06-22.beyerM88.connor.30865.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 159 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sound quality is good [20]
- **gd86-06-22.neumann-fleck.unknown.7281.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 1.75/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd1986-06-22.148481.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 168 min [7]
- **gd86-06-22.sbd.lai.388.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 155 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [16]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has small snaps and dropouts on discs 1 and 3, all fixable with editing software; Reviewer's earlier audience tape had a strange echo [17][24]

## Around the show

- Sunday afternoon show closing a weekend run of Berkeley shows [18]
- Falling on the first day of summer, Weir improvised 'Sweet Summertime' lines in Lovelight [19]
- A crowd chant of 'Not Fade Away' and 'We Want Phil' before Box of Rain is missing from this version [21]
- Crosby sat in the grass outside to avoid violating his probation, and people swung on the flagpole [27]
- Many people left during the first encore; fans chanting for Phil to sing were rewarded with a song [27]
- West Coast fans had heard only one Box of Rain since its return, in April at the BCT [19]
- Fire opening a second set is an unusual change; reviewer thinks it is worthwhile for an 1986 show [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-06-22.schoeps.grace-szvetecz.gems.100204.flac16**: taped by Mike Grace and Annie Szvetecz; transferred by Mike Grace and Jamie Waddell; source: Schoeps CMC42 (Spread Omnis, Spaced 3 Feet Apart with 180 degree angle of incidence) -> Grace 18v Mic Preamp -> MOD PCM-F1, Recording Location: Official Tapers… [1]. Also: Transferred by Mike Grace from Betamax PCM tapes via Sony PCM-601ESD into Wavelab at 24bit/44.1kHz; Main difficulty was getting the Betamax tapes to play without dropouts; repacking the tape and tweaking tracking helped [1]
- **gd1986-06-22.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81646.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell MX-90) D [2]. Also: Recorded with Neumann KMi84 mics to PCM, then DAT and CD; cassettes supplied by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [2]
- **gd86-06-22.beyerM88.connor.30865.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Charlie Connor; transferred by Charlie Connor; source: Audience: Beyer Dynamic M88's [3]
- **gd86-06-22.neumann-fleck.unknown.7281.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Randy Fleck; source: Audience: Neumann kmi-84's [4]. Also: Taper used Neumann microphones and early digital PCM equipment for the master recording [23]
- **gd1986-06-22.148481.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [7]. Also: A Schoeps CMC4 MK42 source supplies a 24-second patch in Drums > Space [7]
- **gd86-06-22.sbd.lai.388.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: Soundboard [16]

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Greek Theatre - June 22, 1986](https://www.dead.net/show/june-22-1986) [31]

Many people left during the first encore; fans chanting for Phil to sing were rewarded with a song
Transferred by Mike Grace from Betamax PCM tapes via Sony PCM-601ESD into Wavelab at 24bit/44.1kHz
Main difficulty was getting the Betamax tapes to play without dropouts; repacking the tape and tweaking tracking helped
Recorded with Neumann KMi84 mics to PCM, then DAT and CD; cassettes supplied by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker
Neumann KM84i master cassette from Chris Hecht, transferred by Charlie Miller
A Schoeps CMC4 MK42 source supplies a 24-second patch in Drums > Space
